**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after its parents, see order below).

## What looks good
- The fix is the lathe form of #1019's hop law, small and local to `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`onHole` / `chainRapid` / `chainCut`, lines ~531-555). A rapid that leaves the hole (off centre, or above R) writes `G80` first and is then posted exactly as the stream says, so the tool leaves at the stream's exit Z/X, never at R. The cancel always precedes the first non-cycle move.
- Single hole: golden gains only `G00 X0 Z30` between `G80` and `M9`/`G28 U0 W0`, which is the stream's `ClearancePlane` exit. Line by line that is the only golden change; no other golden moved.
- Last hole before a tool change or section end: the exit rapid already closed the group; `endPreamble` (line 406) still writes `G80` if a group is somehow still open, so no cycle stays active across a tool change or home.
- A cut leaving the hole inside an open group is refused by name rather than dropped. Legacy records with no R keep the old behaviour (documented in `docs/decisions/1011-lathe-cycle-exit.md`).
- `tormach-lathe.cps` writes no canned cycle and already exits at clearance; the new read-back pin covers it too.
- No `.github`, build.rs, Cargo or process-file changes (no PROCESS_VERSION bump needed); no snapshot PNGs; decision file present; no clean-room concerns.

## Stacking and merge order
- Stacked: this branch contains #964 (`issue/906-c-unwind-rate-cap`, still open) and #975 (`issue/966-lathe-c-no-rate`) commits; its own change is the single top commit. Merge #964, then #975, then this PR. Retarget is not needed (all base `main`).
- `git merge-tree` of this head against #1019, #1002, #990 and #975: all clean, no conflicts. #1019 is the mill counterpart and is independent of this file.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- Two consecutive `onCycle` records with no exit rapid between them would skip the positioning block (the `!inCycle` guard, line ~709); the PR notes this as out of scope since a lathe drills one on-centre hole. Worth a follow-up if multi-hole face drilling is added.
- Not exercised end to end: G84/G85 on a lathe (same path as G83).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 1f156d309a5f4b3d6c0bf6c3afd9a80a664f33e0 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (after its parents: #964, then #975, then this PR).

This is the maintainer side's independent review of this PR's own top commit (`1f156d30`, "fix(post): the Fanuc lathe leaves a face-drilled hole at the stream's exit"), judged as a diff against #975's head `7e01f463`. The stacked #964 and #975 commits were already reviewed clean at `d1e1245a` and `7e01f463`. (The earlier marker review on this head was written by the PR's author, so it doesn't count as the independent review.)

## What looks good
- **The defect is real, and the fix only moves the tool farther from the part.** Before: every move after `G83` was swallowed until the section ended. The tool stood at the cycle's initial level (R, Z20 in the golden) when `G28 U0 W0` moved X and Z together. Now `chainRapid` (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` ~546) closes the group on the first rapid that leaves the hole and posts that rapid exactly as the stream gives it, so the tool goes up to Z30 first. Where the control stands after the cycle (X0, Z = R) is where the stream's chain ends: every chain kind in `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs` (drill, peck/deep, tap, bore) finishes at `r_z`. So the first posted move starts from the point the verifier assumed. I checked the cases you would worry about:
  - **Peck / deep:** every peck retract is `<= r_z`, so it stays on the hole and is swallowed (`onHole`, `p.Z <= cycR + EPS`).
  - **Dwell:** P goes on the cycle block only, so the chain is unaffected.
  - **Multiple holes:** a lathe drills on centre only, and the off-axis refusal is unchanged. After an exit, the next hole's approach posts as plain moves, and the `!inCycle` positioning check runs as before.
  - **Last hole / tool change:** the exit has already closed the group. `endPreamble` (~406) still writes `G80` if a group is somehow still open, so there is never a second `G80` and never a cycle left open across `M9`/`G28`.
  - **A hop at or below R** would be swallowed and leave the tool at R, which is higher. That is not a risk.
- **Modal state is unchanged.** `G80` comes before the first plain move, and the move carries its own `G00`. No R/G98/G99 word is added, so the control still returns to the initial level as before. Per-rev feed (`F0.008`) is untouched.
- **A cut that leaves the hole inside an open group is refused by name** (`chainCut`, ~552) and writes no guess. A legacy record with no R keeps the old suppression (`cycR = Infinity`, ~726).
- **Goldens:** one line changed, `+G00 X0 Z30` in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/axial_drill.nc`. It is the stream's ClearancePlane exit, fully explained. No other golden moved, so programs with no face drilling come out byte-identical.
- **Tormach lathe:** `tormach-lathe.cps` has no canned cycle and posts the chain as plain moves. Its goldens already exit at Z30, and the new read-back pin runs on both posts. No other lathe dialect ships. The mill posts are #1019's (issue #994).
- **Revert check reproduced:** with `fanuc-lathe.cps` restored to `7e01f463`, `both_lathe_posts_leave_a_face_drilled_hole_at_the_streams_exit` fails with `"the program leaves its hole at Z20, below the exit Z30"`. With the fix, it passes.
- **Laws:**
  - No unwrap/expect/panic in product code.
  - A CPS file is exempt from the 400-line rule.
  - The new test has its provenance line and gate map.
  - Decision file `docs/decisions/1011-lathe-cycle-exit.md` is present.
  - Clean-room: public RS-274 / handbook semantics only.
  - No build.rs, `.github`, scripts, dependency or process-file changes, so no PROCESS_VERSION bump is needed.
  - No snapshot PNGs, and no CHANGELOG.md edit.
  - The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #1011`.

| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- The chain the motion kernel emits for a bore ends in a *rapid* back to R, while G85 feeds out. That is older than this PR and outside it; the cycle block is what runs on the control.
- G84/G85 are not exercised end to end on the lathe. They take the same `chainRapid`/`chainCut` path that the synthetic refusals test covers for G83.
- Merge order: #964, then #975, then this PR. Each takes `git merge origin/main` if main moves in between.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
